title: What training must public school teachers in Japan complete now that license renewal has been abolished?
description: How Japan replaced teacher license renewal in 2022 with mandatory training records (kenshu rireki) for public school teachers, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Japan abolished teacher license renewal on July 1, 2022. In its place, the Act on Special Provisions concerning Education Public Servants requires the appointing board of education to keep a record of each public school principal's and teacher's training (the kenshu rireki) for training taken from April 1, 2023, and to use it in guidance conversations. Statutory induction, mid-career and remedial training remain mandatory, guided by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology.
keyTakeaways: Act No. 40 of 2022 ended the license renewal system from July 1, 2022: licenses that carried a validity period on that date now have no validity period, and the old 30 hour renewal course requirement no longer applies.

Article 22-5 of the Act on Special Provisions concerning Education Public Servants requires appointing authorities to create a training record for each principal and teacher, covering at least three mandatory categories plus any other activity the authority considers necessary.
The record obligation applies to training taken on or after April 1, 2023, and the record must be used in guidance and advice on professional development under Article 22-6.

Induction training for one year from appointment (Article 23), mid-career training with an individual plan (Article 24) and remedial training limited to one year, extendable to two (Article 25) remain statutory.
MEXT's guideline says records should be kept for a considerable period under each authority's document rules and, where possible, from entry into teaching to the present.
regulator: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), with prefectural and municipal boards of education as appointing authorities
appliesTo: Principals, vice principals, head teachers and teachers at public elementary, junior high, compulsory education, high, secondary and special needs schools
Principals and teachers at public kindergartens and integrated centers for early childhood education and care (yoho renkei gata nintei kodomo en)
Boards of education acting as appointing authorities, training providers and guidance and advice providers
Not covered by the statutory record: temporarily appointed teachers and others excluded by Cabinet Order, although MEXT suggests including them in practice

sections.heading: What happened to teacher license renewal in Japan?

blocks.text: Teacher license renewal was abolished on July 1, 2022 and replaced by a training record and guidance system. The Diet passed the Act Partially Amending the Act on Special Provisions concerning Education Public Servants and the Education Personnel Certification Act on May 11, 2022, and it was promulgated as Act No. 40 of 2022 on May 18, 2022. MEXT's [renewal system archive](https://www.mext.go.jp/a_menu/shotou/koushin/index.htm) describes the renewal system as "developmentally dissolved" (発展的に解消) from July 1, 2022.

Under the old system, introduced on April 1, 2009, licenses first issued from that date carried a 10 year validity period, and teachers had to complete at least 30 hours of license renewal courses within a two year window to keep them valid. Article 3 of the supplementary provisions of Act No. 40 of 2022, as published in the [Education Personnel Certification Act on e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/324AC0000000147), provides that ordinary and special licenses with a validity period in force on the enforcement date have no validity period from that date.

MEXT's [announcement of the law's passage](https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/activity/detail/2022/20220511.html) framed the change as building a new training system matched to individual schools and teachers, together with a revised ministerial guideline on teacher quality and a new guideline for using training records.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the Act on Special Provisions concerning Education Public Servants as published on e-Gov and MEXT guidance as at November 2026. MEXT revised the ministerial guideline on teacher quality indicators on March 9, 2026. Check the primary sources before relying on any article number.

sections.heading: What does the training record (kenshu rireki) obligation require?

blocks.text: Article 22-5(1) of the [Act on Special Provisions concerning Education Public Servants](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/324AC0000000001) (教育公務員特例法, Act No. 1 of 1949) requires the appointing authority to create, for each principal and teacher at a public school, a record of their participation in training and other activities to improve their capabilities. The obligation sits with the board of education, not with the individual teacher.
Article 22-5(2) sets four categories the record is to contain:

items: Training delivered by the training provider (研修実施者実施研修), including induction and mid-career training.
Graduate school courses completed during graduate study leave under Article 26(1).
Accredited courses or correspondence education opened by the appointing authority for which the person earned credits.
Any other capability improvement activity the appointing authority considers necessary.

blocks.text: MEXT's [Guideline on Encouraging Training Through Dialogue Using Training Records](https://www.mext.go.jp/content/20250221-mxt_kyoikujinzai01-000023812_2_1.pdf) (August 2022, partly revised March 2023) treats categories 1 to 3 as records that must always be made, and category 4 as discretionary. It warns that recording must not become an end in itself and that record keeping should be kept simple.

Under Article 2 of the supplementary provisions of Act No. 40 of 2022, Article 22-5 applies to training taken, and courses completed, on or after April 1, 2023. Where a prefectural board is the appointing authority, Article 22-5(3) requires it to share record information with the municipal board that gives guidance and advice.

sections.heading: How must boards of education use training records?

blocks.text: The record must be used to guide each teacher's development. Article 22-6 requires the guidance and advice provider to respond to consultations, provide information on training opportunities and give guidance, and Article 22-6(2) says it must do so based on the teacher's quality indicators and training plan while using the training record information.

The structure above the record is also statutory. Article 22-2 requires the Minister of MEXT to set a guideline for formulating quality indicators. Article 22-3 requires each appointing authority to set quality indicators for principals and teachers by role, experience and aptitude, after consulting a council under Article 22-7. Article 22-4 requires training providers to set a training plan every fiscal year based on those indicators.

MEXT's guideline expects principals to hold the dialogue in practice, typically at the start and end of year personnel evaluation interviews, while noting that the volume of training is not itself reflected in personnel evaluation. Where a teacher, without reasonable grounds, does not attend statutory training or training the plan requires of all eligible staff, the guideline says a duty order (職務命令) to attend may be issued as a last resort.

sections.heading: Which training is mandatory for public school teachers in Japan?

blocks.text: Three forms of training are mandatory by statute: induction training, mid-career training and remedial training. Article 21 also places a general duty on education public servants to "constantly strive for research and self-cultivation" (絶えず研究と修養に努めなければならない) to fulfill their duties, and Article 22 gives them a right to training opportunities.

blocks.text: Under Article 25-2, where the end of remedial training assessment finds instruction is still inadequate, the appointing authority is to take measures including dismissal. That makes remedial training records some of the most consequential in the system, and the assessment process requires the views of experts and local guardians under Article 25(5).

sections.heading: What should a training record contain and how long should it be kept?

blocks.text: The Act sets the categories; MEXT's guideline leaves the fields and retention period to each appointing authority. It lists candidate fields from which authorities decide mandatory and desirable items: training name, content, organizer, fiscal year, timing, period and hours, location (or online), attribute (all staff or voluntary), format (in person, on demand, live online, correspondence), relationship to the quality indicators, reflections, and training reports.

On retention, the guideline says records are kept "for a considerable period" (相当期間) under each authority's rules for administrative documents and, as far as possible, from a teacher's entry into the profession to the present. Records may be held in an information system, electronic files or paper, and MEXT recommends that teachers and school leaders can view their own records at any time where a system is used.

blocks.text: Organizations outside Japan's public school system will recognize the pattern: a role-based indicator set, an annual plan derived from it, and a per-person record reviewed in conversation. The same structure is described in [how to build a competency framework](/guides/how-to-build-a-competency-framework) and [how to run a training gap analysis](/guides/how-to-run-a-training-gap-analysis), and record retention questions are covered in [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records).

sections.heading: Do these rules apply to private schools and temporary teachers?

blocks.text: The statutory record applies to principals and teachers at public schools, because the Act governs education public servants employed by local government. Article 2 defines public schools as schools under Article 1 of the School Education Act and integrated early childhood centers established by local public entities, so private school teachers are outside the Article 22-5 obligation.

MEXT's guideline confirms that temporarily appointed teachers are not covered by the statutory record and dialogue, but suggests appointing authorities include them in practice using personnel evaluation interviews. For an employer, the abolition of renewal means a teacher's license no longer lapses for missed courses; the compliance question has moved to whether the board's records and guidance process meet the Act. Related Japanese workplace duties are covered in the [Industrial Safety and Health Act training page](/regulations/japan-industrial-safety-and-health-act-training) and the [power harassment prevention page](/regulations/japan-power-harassment-prevention-obligations).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models quality indicators as a framework of role and career stage outcomes, then links each training activity and record entry to the indicator it develops. That gives boards and schools a record that can be used in guidance conversations rather than a list of course titles.

faqs.q: Did teacher licenses that had expired before July 2022 come back into force?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The supplementary provisions remove the validity period only from licenses that were in force on the July 1, 2022 enforcement date. MEXT published separate guidance on the handling of licenses issued up to June 30, 2022, and anyone whose license lapsed earlier should check with the prefectural board of education that manages it.

faqs.q: Does every training session have to be recorded?
faqs.a: No. Training by the training provider, graduate study leave courses and accredited courses opened by the appointing authority must be recorded. Other activities are recorded only where the appointing authority considers them necessary, and MEXT's guideline suggests voluntary training be recorded selectively on the teacher's own report.

faqs.q: Is the training record used for performance ratings?
faqs.a: MEXT's guideline says the record is mainly for guidance conversations and that the amount of training is not directly reflected in personnel evaluation, although the abilities and results a teacher shows after training can be evaluated. Authorities may use records for other personnel purposes once they set document management rules specifying that use.

faqs.q: Who holds the training record when a teacher moves to another prefecture?
faqs.a: The current appointing authority has no duty to recreate records made by a previous authority. MEXT's guideline says it is desirable, where possible and consistent with personal information law, to obtain the earlier record from the previous authority or from the teacher.

Act No. 40 of 2022 (promulgated May 18, 2022) took effect July 1, 2022; supplementary provision Article 3 provides that licenses with a validity period in force on the enforcement date have no validity period thereafter

Article 22-5 requires the appointing authority to create a training record per principal and teacher with four listed categories; under supplementary provisions Articles 1(2) and 2 of Act No. 40 of 2022 it applies to training taken from April 1, 2023; Article 22-5(3) requires prefectural boards to share record information

Article 22-6(2) requires guidance and advice to be based on indicators and training plans and to use the training record; Articles 22-2, 22-3, 22-4 and 22-7 set the guideline, indicators, annual training plan and council

Article 23 induction training for one year from appointment with a mentor teacher; Article 24 mid-career training with individual plan; Article 25 remedial training not exceeding one year, extendable to two; Article 25-2 dismissal or other measures

MEXT guideline (August 2022, partly revised March 2023): categories 1 to 3 must be recorded; candidate record fields; retention for a considerable period under document rules, ideally from entry to present; temporary appointees not covered by statute; duty order as last resort; training volume not directly reflected in personnel evaluation
